title: Kamat Steels v. Rane Constructions: cheque dishonour ₹6.8L
summary: Two cheques issued against supply of TMT bars returned 'funds insufficient'.

documents.text:
Cheque No. 004512 dated 02 August 2026 for Rs. 6,80,000 drawn on Bank of India, Margao was returned unpaid with the bank return memo stating funds insufficient on 22 August 2026.
The complainant sent a statutory demand notice under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act by speed post on 05 September 2026, within 30 days of the dishonour memo.
Postal tracking report shows the notice was delivered to the drawer on 08 September 2026.
The cheque was issued towards a legally enforceable debt for TMT bars supplied under tax invoices dated June 2026.
No payment was made within 15 days of receipt of the notice and the cause of action arose on 23 September 2026.

title: Dsouza v. Coastal Motors: defective SUV, consumer complaint
forum_hint: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, North Goa
summary: New SUV developed repeated gearbox failure within warranty; dealer refused replacement.

documents.text:
The complainant purchased the vehicle under tax invoice dated 14 October 2025 for Rs. 14,20,000 and paid through bank loan EMI.
Job cards dated 03 December 2025, 19 January 2026 and 02 April 2026 record the same gearbox defect within the warranty period.
The complainant raised a complaint to the seller by email and customer care ticket number CM-77821.
The dealer replied that the defect was due to driving habits, which the complainant disputes.
An independent expert report dated 10 May 2026 confirms a manufacturing defect in the transmission.

voice.original_text: हांव गाडी घेतली ती तीन फावट वर्कशॉपांत गेली, पूण गियरबॉक्स अजून बरो जावंक ना.
voice.english_translation: I bought the car and it went to the workshop three times, but the gearbox is still not fixed.

title: Naik v. Naik: mutual consent divorce
forum_hint: Family Court, North Goa at Mapusa
summary: Parties living separately since March 2025; settlement on alimony and custody reached in mediation.

documents.text:
The marriage was solemnised on 12 May 2016 and registered; the marriage certificate is on record.
The parties have been living separately since 15 March 2025 and have not cohabited since.
A mediation and counselling session at the court-annexed centre produced signed settlement terms on custody and a one-time alimony.
Both parties seek waiver of the six-month cooling period under Section 13B(2).

voice.original_text: आम्ही दोघेही एक वर्षापासून वेगळे राहतो आणि मुलांच्या ताब्याबद्दल आमचे एकमत झाले आहे.
voice.english_translation: We have both been living separately for a year and we have agreed on custody of the children.

title: Gauns v. Gauns: maintenance under BNSS s.144
summary: Wife and minor child deserted; respondent earns from a mining transport business.

documents.text:
The applicant is the legally wedded wife of the respondent; the marriage proof and birth certificate of the child are on record.
The respondent stopped paying household expenses and deserted the applicant in April 2026, amounting to neglect or refusal to maintain.
The respondent's income from a truck transport business is about Rs. 85,000 per month as per bank statement extracts.
School fees and medical bills for the child are annexed as expenses proof.

title: Fernandes (minor) v. Oriental Insurance: MACT claim
forum_hint: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, South Goa
opposite_party: Driver, Owner and Oriental Insurance Co.
summary: 17-year-old pillion rider suffered 40% permanent disability after a speeding bus hit the scooter.

documents.text:
FIR No. 112/2026 was registered at Margao Town police station on 09 July 2026 against the bus driver for rash and negligent driving.
Medical records and a discharge summary from Goa Medical College show compound fracture of the right femur.
A disability certificate issued by the medical board assesses 40% permanent disability of the right lower limb.
The insurance policy of the offending bus with Oriental Insurance was valid on the date of accident.
The claimant was a student; income proof of the parents is filed.

title: Velip v. Goa Ferro Alloys: illegal termination
summary: Machine operator with 6 years' service terminated without notice or retrenchment compensation.

documents.text:
The workman was issued an appointment letter dated 01 June 2019 as machine operator.
Attendance records show continuous service of more than 240 days in each of the last five years.
A termination order dated 30 August 2025 was issued without one month's notice or retrenchment compensation under Section 25F.
Salary slips and PF statements up to August 2025 are on record.
Conciliation before the Assistant Labour Commissioner failed and a failure report was issued.

title: Prabhu v. State of Goa: promotion seniority writ
opposite_party: State of Goa & Directorate of Health Services
summary: Medical officer superseded in promotion; junior officers promoted contrary to recruitment rules.

documents.text:
The impugned order dated 10 February 2026 promoted three officers junior to the petitioner.
The petitioner submitted a representation to the Secretary, Health on 25 February 2026 which remains undecided.
The service record and seniority list of 2024 show the petitioner at serial no. 4.
The recruitment rules require promotion on seniority-cum-merit.
Similarly placed comparator officers with lower ACR grading were promoted.

title: State v. Mandrekar: anticipatory bail, cheating
forum_hint: Sessions Court, North Goa at Panaji
summary: Real-estate agent apprehends arrest after complaint alleging cheating on a flat booking.

documents.text:
FIR registered on 14 Feb 2025 under IPC 420, IPC 406 and CrPC 438 relief is sought by the accused.
The complainant alleges that Rs. 12,00,000 paid as booking amount was not refunded.
The dispute is essentially civil and the accused has offered to deposit the amount.
The accused has no prior conviction for the same offence and has cooperated with the investigation.
The offence maximum punishment is up to 7 years.

title: Comunidade de Taleigão v. Shirodkar: eviction of mundkar plot
summary: Arrears of ground rent and sub-letting of a leased comunidade plot.

documents.text:
The respondent holds the plot under a registered lease deed dated 1998 from the comunidade.
A notice to quit under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was served on 05 January 2024.
Arrears of rent of Rs. 1,86,000 remain unpaid since 2021.
The respondent has sub-let part of the premises to a hardware shop without written consent.
Rent receipts up to 2020 are on record.

voice.original_text: भाटकाराक भाडें दिवंक ना आनी दुकान दुसऱ्याक भाड्यान दिलां.
voice.english_translation: He has not paid rent to the bhatkar and has let the shop to someone else.

title: Desai Exports v. Bharat Shipping: s.11 arbitrator appointment
summary: Charter-party demurrage dispute; respondent ignored the notice invoking arbitration.

documents.text:
Clause 32 of the charter party dated 04 March 2024 is an arbitration clause providing for a sole arbitrator seated at Panaji.
A notice invoking arbitration under section 21 was served on 20 November 2025.
The respondent did not reply or concur in the name of an arbitrator within 30 days.
The statement of claim quantifies demurrage at Rs. 42,50,000.
Correspondence by email shows the dispute was raised in 2025.

title: Estate of late A. Pereira: probate of will
summary: Executor seeks probate; one heir alleges suspicious circumstances.

documents.text:
The death certificate records the death of Antonio Pereira on 18 June 2025 at Margao.
The last will dated 02 February 2023 bequeaths the Benaulim property to the petitioner.
Two attesting witnesses signed the will and one attesting witness is available to depose.
Property records including Form I & XIV and bank account statements are annexed.
One heir has not given a no-objection and alleges the testator was unwell.

title: Konkan Spice Co. v. Spyce Konkan: trademark passing off
summary: Deceptively similar mark and trade dress on masala packets sold in Goa and Karnataka.

documents.text:
The plaintiff holds a registration certificate for the word mark KONKAN SPICE in Class 30.
Invoices from 2009 onward establish prior use and goodwill in Goa.
A trap purchase on 02 May 2026 produced infringing packets with a deceptively similar mark.
Annual sales figures exceed Rs. 3 crore with advertisement expenses on record.
A cease and desist notice was sent on 10 May 2026 and ignored.

title: Salgaonkar v. Ghanekar: unregistered agreement, possession suit
summary: Plaintiff in possession under an unregistered agreement of sale with payment trail.

documents.text:
The plaintiff entered possession on 12 May 2014 under an agreement of sale which is not registered.
Stamp duty was paid on the agreement as per the stamp office receipt.
Electricity bills and house tax receipts in the plaintiff's name show possession since 2014.
The Form I & XIV extract still shows the defendant's father as occupant.
Payment trail to seller of Rs. 9,00,000 through bank transfers is on record.

title: Shetty Hardware v. Kunkolienkar: recovery of price of goods
summary: Unpaid invoices for building material; part-payment and balance confirmation on record.

documents.text:
Tax invoices dated January to March 2024 record supply of cement and steel worth Rs. 3,40,000.
Delivery challans are acknowledged by the defendant's site supervisor.
A part payment of Rs. 60,000 was made by NEFT on 30 March 2024.
The defendant signed a balance confirmation acknowledging the outstanding in June 2025.
There is no written contract; supply was against oral orders confirmed on WhatsApp.

title: Moot: Ramesh v. Sunil (Goa Law School moot problem)
summary: Moot problem on whether a security cheque attracts s.138 liability.

documents.text:
Sunil issued a cheque to Ramesh as security for a friendly loan of Rs. 2,00,000.
The cheque was presented and returned with the memo funds insufficient on 01 August 2026.
Ramesh issued a demand notice under section 138 within 30 days.
Sunil claims the cheque was a security cheque and no legally enforceable debt existed on the date of presentation.

title: Pai v. Lotus Builders: delay in possession of flat
forum_hint: State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Goa
summary: Builder delayed possession by 3 years; homebuyer seeks refund with interest.

documents.text:
The agreement for sale dated 2019 promised possession by September 2022.
Possession has not been offered and construction is incomplete as per photographs dated 2025.
Payment receipts show Rs. 48,00,000 paid through bank loan.
The complainant sent a complaint to the seller and a legal notice in September 2025.

voice.original_text: ಮೂರು ವರ್ಷ ಕಳೆದರೂ ಫ್ಲ್ಯಾಟ್ ಕೊಟ್ಟಿಲ್ಲ, ನಮ್ಮ ಹಣ ಬಡ್ಡಿಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ವಾಪಸ್ ಬೇಕು.
voice.english_translation: Even after three years the flat has not been handed over; we want our money back with interest.

title: Mandovi Marine v. Coastline Fuels: s.12A commercial suit ₹27L
summary: Breach of bunkering contract; mediation non-starter report obtained.

documents.text:
The master services agreement dated 2023 is a written contract for marine bunkering.
Tax invoices and delivery receipts for April 2025 total Rs. 27,40,000.
Pre-institution mediation under section 12A was attempted and a non-starter report was issued on 18 April 2025.
Email correspondence shows the defendant admitted the delivery but disputed the rate.

title: Hegde Traders v. Basavaraj: cheque bounce, Belagavi
summary: Cheque for cashew consignment dishonoured; complaint filed within time.

documents.text:
Cheque dated 20 May 2026 for Rs. 4,10,000 was returned with the memo exceeds arrangement.
A demand notice under section 138 was sent within 30 days by registered post with acknowledgment card.
The debt arose from cashew consignments under tax invoices, a legally enforceable debt.
The complaint was filed within time on 11 June 2026.

title: Kulkarni v. Kulkarni: interim maintenance, Kolhapur
summary: Wife seeks interim maintenance; husband is a software engineer in Pune.

documents.text:
Marriage proof is on record and the parties have one child.
The respondent stopped sending money from March 2026, amounting to neglect or refusal to maintain.
The respondent's salary is Rs. 1,80,000 per month as per salary slips.
An income and asset affidavit in the Rajnesh format is filed by the applicant.

title: State v. Shaikh: regular bail, Hubballi
summary: Undertrial in custody for 13 months; co-accused already on bail.

documents.text:
FIR and chargesheet under sections 323, 504 and 506 IPC and 379 IPC have been filed.
The offence maximum punishment is under 7 years and the trial has not commenced.
The co-accused was granted bail; the applicant seeks parity.
The applicant has no prior conviction for the same offence.
